Full summary: Ultracode 72-agent adversarial review of the field-authored twining_triage spec (~/Downloads/2026-07-22-twining-triage-spec.md). Verdict: gap is real, fit confirmed (yes-with-conditions), spec NOT buildable as written — 5 load-bearing defects. Full report: ~/Downloads/2026-07-22-twining-triage-spec-REVIEW.md
Decisions: Concluded twining_triage belongs in twining-mcp core as an engine-owned read-model over building it consumer-side — the classification depends on engine invariants (the #40 relates_to resolution convention, supersession chains, provisional semantics) that a consumer wrapper over the HTTP API would duplicate and silently drift from; conditions: dashboard-first surfacing, MCP tool gated behind full_surface initially (not default surface as spec §6 mandates), no freestanding heuristic stakes scalar (follow the staleness-score named-signals precedent), and a pre-declared field-data exit test per the twining_handoff deprecation precedent; Chose to re-run 5 of 8 adversarial review dimensions in a second workflow round after discovering the Workflow args object was stringified by the harness, making args.spec resolve to undefined — round-1 results for those dimensions were ungrounded in the actual spec text; the 3 dimensions whose agents independently located the spec, plus the fact-checks of verbatim-quoted claims, were kept
Findings: warning: triage spec §5 (its self-declared most important section) analyzes only the legacy file backend — SQLite is the v2 default, where the decision index is a read-time projection over full records: adding reversible is a one-line projection change in sqlite-stores.ts getIndex(), no migration/backfill/degraded machinery needed; an implementer following §5 literally would patch only the file writer and leave the default backend permanently degraded; warning: the spec's ratify queue has no exit condition — DecisionStatus has no ratified state and approving leaves a decision active+irreversible, in queue forever; the repo already ships the ratification state machine (twining_reconsider active→provisional, twining_promote provisional→active) which the spec inverts and omits from its §9 tool list; warning: 'open need' is undefined in the spec but the repo has a canonical predicate (issue #40: resolved when a later entry back-references via relates_to, archiver.ts:34-63) — any triage implementation must reuse it or triage and archiving will disagree about which needs are live; spec's handoff pillar builds on twining_handoff/twining_acknowledge, both deprecated for v3 removal with zero field usage; real handoffs are artifact posts, absent from the spec's TriageItem kinds — a gating drop-vs-invest decision is needed before any handoff-lane work; spec's default stakes formula is sign-inverted for its stated purpose (rewards HIGH confidence +0.3, so the lead reviews agents' most-confident irreversible decisions first, contradicting 'ranked by how expensive to get wrong'), exceeds its declared [0,1] range (max 1.1), and gives handoffs no term at all; combined with §4.2's contractual golden-test ordering in a published semver package this would freeze a wrong formula — resolve stakes-null vs advisory-ordering before v1; file-backend index backfill claim in spec §5 is false: only DecisionStore.create() writes full index entries (updateStatus/linkCommit patch single fields), so 'populated on next write' never happens for existing decisions; measured full-record read cost is ~3.3ms for 170 decisions (~45ms extrapolated to the 2,180-decision field store) — pure Option C is likely sufficient; on default installs every drain action the triage spec names (twining_acknowledge/override/reconsider/promote) is fullSurface-gated while full_surface defaults false — a default-surface triage tool shows a queue nothing in the session can act on
